checks.prompt: What is a cross-connection in a water system?
choices: A valve that links two treated water storage tanks to each other
A fitting that couples two sections of the same water main pipe
A link from drinking water to a source of contamination
A cross-shaped pipe fitting used where two water mains meet
checks.explanation: A cross-connection links drinking water to a possible contaminant, so a pressure drop (backsiphonage) or higher pressure on the other side (backpressure) can move that contaminant backward into the clean pipe. The "A valve that links two treated water storage tanks to each other" choice described an ordinary valve between two clean sources. The "A fitting that couples two sections of the same water main pipe" choice described a coupling, which is routine pipe work. The "A cross-shaped pipe fitting used where two water mains meet" choice read the name literally as the shape of a fitting.

checks.prompt: Which gas is greenish-yellow, irritates the eyes and lungs and sinks to low areas?
choices: Methane
Ammonia
Nitrogen
Chlorine
checks.explanation: Chlorine is a heavy, greenish-yellow, irritating gas, so it collects in pits and low rooms. The "Methane" choice picked a colorless flammable gas that rises. The "Ammonia" choice picked a colorless, pungent gas that is lighter than air. The "Nitrogen" choice picked a colorless gas that is not irritating and does not match the description.

checks.prompt: What is the purpose of an eyewash station or safety shower?
choices: To flush a chemical off the eyes or body quickly
To neutralize the chemical by reacting with it
To give an injured worker a drink of clean water
To rinse tools and equipment after a chemical spill
checks.explanation: These stations dilute and wash off a chemical quickly; time to reach them matters. The "To neutralize the chemical by reacting with it" choice believed the water cancels the chemical, but it only dilutes and removes it. The "To give an injured worker a drink of clean water" choice chose an unrelated first aid purpose. The "To rinse tools and equipment after a chemical spill" choice chose a cleaning purpose for equipment made for people.

checks.prompt: A fictional operator sees crusting and a damp stain around a chemical line fitting. The best classification is:
choices: A cosmetic issue to note at the next repainting
A possible leak to report before it grows
A normal trace of the last delivery
A spill that matters if it reaches a drain
checks.explanation: Crusting and stains are early signs that a fitting is leaking, and early reporting prevents a larger release. The "A cosmetic issue to note at the next repainting" choice treated early leak evidence as a surface-appearance problem. The "A normal trace of the last delivery" choice assumed dried residue is expected and harmless. The "A spill that matters if it reaches a drain" choice waited for a release to travel before treating it as a problem.

checks.prompt: Why should near misses be reported?
choices: They show which workers are being careless
They are reported when equipment is damaged
They reveal hazards that could hurt someone
They prove the safety program has failed
checks.explanation: A near miss is a free warning: the same conditions can injure someone later. The "They show which workers are being careless" choice used the report to assign blame, which discourages reporting. The "They are reported when equipment is damaged" choice limited reporting to events with damage, which misses most near misses. The "They prove the safety program has failed" choice assumed a report is a verdict on the program instead of useful information.

checks.prompt: Why are upright compressed gas cylinders secured, with valve caps on, when not in use?
choices: Upright cylinders hold more gas than ones lying flat
The cap keeps the cylinder label clean and dry
Chains keep the cylinder cool in warm weather
A fall or valve damage can cause a gas release
checks.explanation: Securing the cylinder and covering the valve protects against falls and valve damage that cause a release. The "Upright cylinders hold more gas than ones lying flat" choice assumed position changes how much a cylinder holds, but the reason is protection from falls. The "The cap keeps the cylinder label clean and dry" choice chose a label-protection reason instead of valve protection. The "Chains keep the cylinder cool in warm weather" choice chose a cooling effect that chains do not provide.

finalAssessment.prompt: A fictional crew at Marlow Creek must clean tanks with a solvent. The supervisor offers a water-based cleaner that does the job with less hazard. This choice is:
choices: Substitution, swapping in a safer material
Elimination, removing the cleaning task from the job
An administrative control, changing the work rule
An engineering control, adding ventilation
finalAssessment.explanation: Swapping a hazardous material for a safer one is substitution, the second step down from elimination. The "Elimination, removing the cleaning task from the job" choice assumed the task disappears, but the cleaning still happens. The "An administrative control, changing the work rule" choice treated a material swap as a change to procedure. The "An engineering control, adding ventilation" choice described a different control that this scenario does not use.

finalAssessment.prompt: A fictional operator plans work in the Alder Bend wet well. The wet well is a permit-required space and was clear a week ago. Why are testing and a permit still needed?
choices: The permit proves the space was safe when it was last entered
Conditions change between visits, so air must be rechecked
Testing is needed when a strong odor is noticed in the space
The permit replaces the need for an attendant at the opening
finalAssessment.explanation: The air in a space changes, so the current work needs current testing and a current permit. The "The permit proves the space was safe when it was last entered" choice treated a permit as a lasting guarantee instead of a current check. The "Testing is needed when a strong odor is noticed in the space" choice made testing depend on smell, which is not a dependable warning. The "The permit replaces the need for an attendant at the opening" choice treated paperwork as a substitute for a person posted at the opening.

finalAssessment.prompt: A fictional crew at Pine Hollow digs beside a driveway used by trucks, and rain fell overnight. Which combination most raises the cave-in risk?
choices: A clean cut face, shallow depth and a dry surface
Dry, firm soil, level ground and no nearby traffic
Vibration, added load and wet, soft soil
Painted marks, good lighting and clear signage
finalAssessment.explanation: Water, vibration and added weight all push a wall toward failure. The "A clean cut face, shallow depth and a dry surface" choice chose conditions that lower risk instead of raising it. The "Dry, firm soil, level ground and no nearby traffic" choice chose stable conditions. The "Painted marks, good lighting and clear signage" choice chose conditions that help visibility but do not change wall stability.

finalAssessment.prompt: A fictional plant stores sodium hypochlorite on a pallet beside a pallet of acid, separated by a low aisle. Why is this layout a concern?
choices: Each would lose strength in shared air
Hypochlorite needs more floor space than acid
The pallets would be hard to count
A leak could mix them and release toxic gas
finalAssessment.explanation: Acid and hypochlorite release chlorine gas when they meet, so each needs its own contained area. The "Each would lose strength in shared air" choice chose an aging effect instead of the gas hazard. The "Hypochlorite needs more floor space than acid" choice chose a space reason that does not address safety. The "The pallets would be hard to count" choice chose an inventory reason that does not address safety.

finalAssessment.prompt: In the hierarchy of controls, which is the last line of defence, used when stronger controls cannot remove the hazard?
choices: Engineering controls such as guards
Personal protective equipment
Substitution of a safer material
Elimination of the hazard
finalAssessment.explanation: PPE sits last because it leaves the hazard in place and depends on correct selection, fit and use. The "Engineering controls such as guards" choice placed a stronger, upper-level control at the bottom of the ranking. The "Substitution of a safer material" choice placed a strong upper-level control at the bottom of the ranking. The "Elimination of the hazard" choice placed the strongest control at the bottom of the ranking.

finalAssessment.prompt: What is the main purpose of mechanical ventilation of a permit-required space?
choices: To cover odors so entrants feel comfortable
To replace atmospheric testing during the job
To dilute hazardous air and bring in fresh air
To cool the space for entrants while they work
finalAssessment.explanation: Ventilation supports air quality and works together with testing, not instead of it. The "To cover odors so entrants feel comfortable" choice treated ventilation as odor masking. The "To replace atmospheric testing during the job" choice believed airflow makes monitoring unnecessary. The "To cool the space for entrants while they work" choice chose comfort over atmosphere control.

finalAssessment.prompt: A fictional crew lowers a prefabricated box into a trench and works inside it. This protection method is called:
choices: Sloping
Shoring
Dewatering
Shielding
finalAssessment.explanation: A trench box or shield protects workers if a wall collapses, but it does not hold the walls back. The "Sloping" choice described cutting the walls back, not placing a box. The "Shoring" choice described bracing the walls, which holds soil in place instead of protecting workers inside a box. The "Dewatering" choice described removing water, which is not a cave-in protection system.

finalAssessment.prompt: Which pair of chemicals could form irritating chloramine vapors if they mix?
choices: Hypochlorite and ammonia
Caustic and liquid polymer
Alum and dry polymer
Fluoride and caustic soda
finalAssessment.explanation: Chlorine products react with ammonia to form chloramine compounds, which is why they are stored apart. The "Caustic and liquid polymer" choice picked a pair that does not produce chloramines. The "Alum and dry polymer" choice picked two treatment chemicals that do not react to form chloramines. The "Fluoride and caustic soda" choice picked a pair without a chlorine source.

finalAssessment.prompt: A fictional operator finds an unlabelled drum in the chemical room. Which response fits hazard communication?
choices: Smell the contents to identify it
Treat it as plain water and use it for rinsing
Leave it closed, keep others away, report it
Pour a sample into a small labelled bottle for testing
finalAssessment.explanation: An unlabelled container is an unknown hazard: leave it closed, keep others away and report it. The "Smell the contents to identify it" choice tried to identify an unknown with the nose, which exposes the operator to the hazard. The "Treat it as plain water and use it for rinsing" choice assumed the contents are harmless without evidence. The "Pour a sample into a small labelled bottle for testing" choice opened and handled an unknown product, which spreads the hazard.

finalAssessment.prompt: A fictional gas meter reads 4,000 ppm of a toxic gas. Using 10,000 ppm = 1 percent by volume, the reading in percent by volume is:
choices: 40 percent
4 percent
0.04 percent
0.4 percent
finalAssessment.explanation: 4,000 / 10,000 = 0.4 percent; ppm is a much larger number than percent, so the answer should be small. The "40 percent" choice used 100 ppm for each percent instead of 10,000. The "4 percent" choice divided by 1,000 instead of 10,000. The "0.04 percent" choice divided by 100,000 instead of 10,000.

finalAssessment.prompt: A fictional trench is 7 ft deep. Using 1 ft = 0.3048 m, the depth in metres is:
finalAssessment.explanation: 7 x 0.3048 = 2.13 m; feet are the larger number, so the metre value should be smaller. The "22.97 m" choice divided by 0.3048 instead of multiplying. The "2.31 m" choice used 0.33 for the conversion factor. The "0.04 m" choice divided the factor by the depth.

finalAssessment.prompt: A fictional operator hears a hiss and sees a greenish haze near the chlorine cylinder room. Which response matches awareness-level training?
choices: Walk toward the haze to look for the leak source
Leave, warn others and call the emergency contact
Open a window and keep working at your task
Tighten the valve without protection or training
finalAssessment.explanation: An untrained operator moves away, warns others and calls for trained responders; the facility plan governs the rest. The "Walk toward the haze to look for the leak source" choice approached the release, which adds an exposure and a possible victim. The "Open a window and keep working at your task" choice treated a release as a ventilation chore. The "Tighten the valve without protection or training" choice attempted a repair without training or equipment.

finalAssessment.prompt: A fictional operator needs to know which gloves suit a product. Which SDS section lists engineering controls and suitable PPE?
choices: The physical and chemical properties section
The stability and reactivity section
The toxicological information section
Exposure controls and personal protection
finalAssessment.explanation: The section on exposure controls and personal protection names the engineering controls and the PPE suited to the product. The "The physical and chemical properties section" choice chose the section with appearance and boiling point, which does not name protection. The "The stability and reactivity section" choice chose the section on what the product reacts with, not what to wear. The "The toxicological information section" choice chose the section on health effects data, which does not recommend equipment.

finalAssessment.prompt: A fictional operator smells rotten eggs at a lift station, then notices the smell has gone though work continues. The best interpretation is:
choices: Smell may be dulled, so leave and have the air tested
The gas has cleared because the smell faded away
The gas moved to the top where it is no longer harmful
A weak smell means work can continue as planned
finalAssessment.explanation: Hydrogen sulfide can deaden the sense of smell, so a vanished smell is a reason to stop work, move to fresh air, report it and have trained people test the air with instruments before work resumes. The "The gas has cleared because the smell faded away" choice read a fading smell as a clearing atmosphere. The "The gas moved to the top where it is no longer harmful" choice assumed gas that moves is no longer a hazard. The "A weak smell means work can continue as planned" choice treated odor strength as a safety measure.

finalAssessment.prompt: A fictional trench has a ladder in it. What is the ladder for?
choices: Supporting the trench wall against soil
Giving workers a safe way out nearby
Providing a place to store tools and pipe
Replacing the need for cave-in protection
finalAssessment.explanation: A ladder lets workers leave quickly; it does not protect against a collapse. The "Supporting the trench wall against soil" choice treated an exit as wall support. The "Providing a place to store tools and pipe" choice chose a storage use that adds clutter in the way out. The "Replacing the need for cave-in protection" choice believed a way out removes the cave-in hazard.

finalAssessment.prompt: A fictional plant feeds chlorine at a steady 12 lb/day and holds 96 lb of net chlorine. At that feed rate, the supply lasts:
choices: 1,152 days
0.125 days
8 days
84 days
finalAssessment.explanation: 96 lb / 12 lb per day = 8 days; pounds divided by pounds per day gives days. The "1,152 days" choice multiplied pounds by pounds per day. The "0.125 days" choice divided the feed rate by the pounds on hand. The "84 days" choice subtracted 12 from 96 instead of dividing.

finalAssessment.prompt: A fictional site scores risk as severity times likelihood, each on a 1 to 5 scale. A worn stair tread has severity 3 and likelihood 4. A missing belt guard has severity 5 and likelihood 2. Which ranking is correct?
choices: Stair tread 12 ranks above belt guard 10
Belt guard ranks first because its severity is highest
The two tie at 7 because each pair adds to 7
Belt guard 10 ranks above a stair total of 7
finalAssessment.explanation: 3 x 4 = 12 and 5 x 2 = 10, so the stair tread scores higher; both still need action. The "Belt guard ranks first because its severity is highest" choice ranked by severity alone and ignored likelihood. The "The two tie at 7 because each pair adds to 7" choice added the two scores instead of multiplying. The "Belt guard 10 ranks above a stair total of 7" choice multiplied one pair but added the other.

finalAssessment.prompt: Which atmospheric hazard is an absence rather than a substance and gives no smell or color warning?
choices: Hydrogen sulfide gas
Oxygen deficiency
Chlorine
Ammonia
finalAssessment.explanation: Low oxygen is the lack of a gas, so there is nothing to see or smell, which is why instruments are needed. The "Hydrogen sulfide gas" choice picked a toxic gas that has a recognisable odor at low levels. The "Chlorine" choice picked a gas with a strong odor and a greenish color. The "Ammonia" choice picked a gas with a sharp, easily noticed odor.

finalAssessment.prompt: A fictional operator finds a coworker's lock and tag on a pump disconnect. What does this mean?
choices: The tag is a reminder that the pump is due for service later
The pump is out of service and any crew member may remove the lock
The coworker is working on the pump and will remove the lock
The pump is ready for a trial start after maintenance
finalAssessment.explanation: A lock and tag mean someone is working on the equipment and the lock stays until its owner removes it; do not operate or remove it. The "The tag is a reminder that the pump is due for service later" choice read a warning device as a work reminder. The "The pump is out of service and any crew member may remove the lock" choice assumed anyone may take off another worker's lock. The "The pump is ready for a trial start after maintenance" choice read a stop signal as permission to start.

finalAssessment.prompt: A fictional operator finds a cut fence and an unlocked chemical room. What is the best response?
choices: Repair the fence at the next scheduled work day
Ignore it because cameras are installed
Post a photo of the damage on social media
Report it promptly and secure the area
finalAssessment.explanation: Security gaps at treatment sites can become chemical or contamination hazards, so report them promptly. The "Repair the fence at the next scheduled work day" choice delayed a security gap that is open now. The "Ignore it because cameras are installed" choice assumed cameras replace locks and a response. The "Post a photo of the damage on social media" choice shared sensitive site information publicly.

alternateFinalAssessment.prompt: A fictional crew at Cedarline finds a missing guard on a belt drive. They replace it before the drive is used again. This action is best described as:
choices: Restoring an engineering control at the machine
Adding PPE for workers near the belt hazard
Posting a warning sign as an administrative control
Substituting a safer drive in place of the belt
alternateFinalAssessment.explanation: A guard is a physical barrier between the person and the moving part, the definition of an engineering control. The "Adding PPE for workers near the belt hazard" choice described worker equipment, but the guard works at the machine. The "Posting a warning sign as an administrative control" choice described a sign, but a guard is a physical barrier. The "Substituting a safer drive in place of the belt" choice described replacing the drive, which did not happen.

alternateFinalAssessment.prompt: Why do entrants in a permit-required space usually wear a harness connected to a lifeline?
choices: To let the entrant climb out alone without help from the attendant
To allow retrieval from outside without sending in a second person
To hold the gas meter and radio close against the entrant's chest
To replace ventilation and atmospheric testing once the entrant is in
alternateFinalAssessment.explanation: A harness and lifeline let the attendant pull an entrant out from outside, so rescue does not mean sending in another person who could be overcome. The "To let the entrant climb out alone without help from the attendant" choice treated the lifeline as a climbing aid, but its job is retrieval. The "To hold the gas meter and radio close against the entrant's chest" choice treated it as a holder for equipment. The "To replace ventilation and atmospheric testing once the entrant is in" choice treated it as a substitute for testing and ventilation, which it is not.

alternateFinalAssessment.prompt: A fictional crew at Pine Hollow lifts a pump with a hoist. Which practice fits crane and hoist awareness?
choices: Stand beside the load to steady it with one hand as it rises
Treat the rated capacity as a guide that a short lift may exceed
Inspect hook and sling first and keep people out from under the load
Let any nearby coworker give signals while the operator watches elsewhere
alternateFinalAssessment.explanation: Inspecting the hook and sling and keeping people clear of the suspended load addresses the two main failures: broken gear and a falling load. The "Stand beside the load to steady it with one hand as it rises" choice put a person within reach of a load that can swing or drop. The "Treat the rated capacity as a guide that a short lift may exceed" choice treated the rating as a suggestion, but the rating is the limit. The "Let any nearby coworker give signals while the operator watches elsewhere" choice split attention, since routine signals come from one agreed signal person the operator watches, although anyone may call a stop.

alternateFinalAssessment.prompt: A fictional plant stores concentrated hydrogen peroxide for odor control. Which storage choice fits recognition-level practice?
choices: A sealed drum parked next to the fuel tank so it is easy to reach
A tightly sealed tank with no vent so no outside air can get in
A drum shared with spare caustic soda to save space on the floor
A vented container made for it, kept apart from fuels
alternateFinalAssessment.explanation: Peroxide can break down and release oxygen and heat, so it is stored in a vented container made for it and kept away from fuels and organic material. The "A sealed drum parked next to the fuel tank so it is easy to reach" choice placed an oxidizer beside fuel, which feeds a fire. The "A tightly sealed tank with no vent so no outside air can get in" choice sealed a product that releases gas as it breaks down, which can burst the tank. The "A drum shared with spare caustic soda to save space on the floor" choice mixed two incompatible products in one place for convenience.

alternateFinalAssessment.prompt: What is a key limit of personal protective equipment as a control?
choices: It removes the hazard at the source
It leaves the hazard in place and relies on correct use
It needs no training once it has been issued to staff
It is not recognised as a valid control layer by safety rules
alternateFinalAssessment.explanation: PPE protects the person but does nothing to the hazard, so its protection depends on the worker. The "It removes the hazard at the source" choice credited PPE with removing the hazard, which belongs to higher controls. The "It needs no training once it has been issued to staff" choice assumed issue is enough, but selection, fit and care need training. The "It is not recognised as a valid control layer by safety rules" choice dismissed PPE entirely, when it is a valid last layer.

alternateFinalAssessment.prompt: A fictional rescue team uses SCBA. What is the key feature of SCBA?
choices: It filters contaminants out of the air around the wearer
It adds oxygen to the room air so entry becomes safe
It carries its own air supply instead of using room air
It is an escape hood that any worker may pick up and use
alternateFinalAssessment.explanation: A self-contained breathing apparatus carries its own air supply, so the wearer does not depend on the air in the space. The "It filters contaminants out of the air around the wearer" choice described a filtering respirator, which cleans room air but makes no oxygen. The "It adds oxygen to the room air so entry becomes safe" choice assumed the apparatus changes the air in the space, but it only supplies the wearer. The "It is an escape hood that any worker may pick up and use" choice ignored that SCBA needs medical clearance, fit testing and training.

alternateFinalAssessment.prompt: A fictional plant's hot work program covers welding near its lift station wet well. Which control fits before the welding starts?
choices: Begin welding at once and watch for stray sparks as the work goes on
Rely on the welding helmet to protect the people working nearby too
Move the gas cylinders next to the repair so they are within easy reach
A hot work permit with gas testing and a fire watch assigned
alternateFinalAssessment.explanation: Sparks can ignite flammable gas or combustibles far from the work, so the facility's hot work permit, gas testing and fire watch come before starting. The "Begin welding at once and watch for stray sparks as the work goes on" choice started the work before checking for gas and combustibles. The "Rely on the welding helmet to protect the people working nearby too" choice assumed the welder's helmet shields bystanders, but arc screens do that. The "Move the gas cylinders next to the repair so they are within easy reach" choice placed cylinders near sparks instead of keeping them secured and away.

alternateFinalAssessment.prompt: A fictional delivery leaves two incompatible chemicals in the same containment tray. This is best classified as:
choices: An incompatibility risk to correct and report
A storage preference with no real safety effect
A task for the next scheduled audit
Acceptable if the containers are sealed
alternateFinalAssessment.explanation: Incompatibles that share containment can mix in a leak, so the situation is corrected and reported. The "A storage preference with no real safety effect" choice treated a reaction hazard as a matter of taste. The "A task for the next scheduled audit" choice delayed a hazard that exists now. The "Acceptable if the containers are sealed" choice assumed sealed containers cannot leak or be damaged.

alternateFinalAssessment.prompt: A fictional label shows a corrosion pictogram (a liquid eating a surface and a hand). The best reading is:
choices: The product is flammable and ignites near heat or sparks
The product may explode when it is heated or shaken
The product can burn skin or eyes or damage metal
The product is a gas held in a pressurized cylinder
alternateFinalAssessment.explanation: The corrosion pictogram signals material that can destroy skin or eyes, or corrode metal, on contact; the hazard statements say which applies. The "The product is flammable and ignites near heat or sparks" choice confused the corrosion pictogram with the flame. The "The product may explode when it is heated or shaken" choice confused it with the exploding bomb pictogram. The "The product is a gas held in a pressurized cylinder" choice confused it with the gas cylinder pictogram.

alternateFinalAssessment.prompt: A fictional meter shows 0.6 percent by volume of a gas. Using 10,000 ppm = 1 percent by volume, the reading in ppm is:
choices: 60 ppm
600 ppm
alternateFinalAssessment.explanation: 0.6 x 10,000 = 6,000 ppm; ppm is the larger number, so converting from percent should make it larger. The "60 ppm" choice used 100 ppm for each percent instead of 10,000. The "600 ppm" choice used 1,000 ppm for each percent. The "60,000 ppm" choice used 100,000 ppm for each percent.

alternateFinalAssessment.prompt: A fictional trench is 9 ft deep. Using 1 ft = 0.3048 m, the depth in metres is:
alternateFinalAssessment.explanation: 9 x 0.3048 = 2.74 m, which is smaller than the depth in feet. The "29.53 m" choice divided by 0.3048 instead of multiplying. The "2.97 m" choice used 0.33 for the conversion factor. The "0.03 m" choice divided the factor by the depth.

alternateFinalAssessment.prompt: A fictional plant feeds chlorine at a steady 14 lb/day and holds 98 lb of net chlorine. At that feed rate, the supply lasts:
choices: 1,372 days
7 days
0.143 days
84 days
alternateFinalAssessment.explanation: 98 lb / 14 lb per day = 7 days. The "1,372 days" choice multiplied pounds by pounds per day. The "0.143 days" choice divided the feed rate by the pounds on hand. The "84 days" choice subtracted 14 from 98 instead of dividing.

alternateFinalAssessment.prompt: A fictional crew at Cedarline sets tools and a pipe section on a catwalk edge above a pump. Which control best stops items dropping on workers below?
choices: A hard hat for the person who is working on the catwalk
A sign asking workers below to walk quickly past the pump
A reminder at the pre-job talk to be careful with the tools
A toe-board along the edge with the area below marked off
alternateFinalAssessment.explanation: A toe-board is a physical barrier that stops items sliding off an elevated edge, and marking the area below keeps people out of the drop zone. The "A hard hat for the person who is working on the catwalk" choice protected only the person above, who is not the one in the drop zone. The "A sign asking workers below to walk quickly past the pump" choice relied on speed instead of removing the hazard. The "A reminder at the pre-job talk to be careful with the tools" choice depended on memory and care, an administrative control that fails when people are busy.

alternateFinalAssessment.prompt: A fictional tank at Willow Gap has been empty and closed for months. Which statement is best?
choices: The air may have changed, so testing and review are needed
An empty tank is safe because nothing is left to release gas
Months of closure let the air clear itself
Opening the hatch briefly makes testing unnecessary
alternateFinalAssessment.explanation: A closed, empty tank can still be low in oxygen or hold gas, so the usual controls apply. The "An empty tank is safe because nothing is left to release gas" choice assumed emptiness removes the hazard, but residue and corrosion still change the air. The "Months of closure let the air clear itself" choice assumed a closed space refreshes the air by itself. The "Opening the hatch briefly makes testing unnecessary" choice treated a short opening as a substitute for testing.

alternateFinalAssessment.prompt: Why does grounding on a power tool or metal enclosure matter?
choices: It stores spare current in the tool so it runs at a steady speed
It gives fault current a path back to the source so a breaker trips
It makes a damaged cord safe enough to use for short jobs in wet areas
It replaces the need for a GFCI on outlets used outdoors in the rain
alternateFinalAssessment.explanation: Grounding gives fault current a low-resistance path back to the source so a breaker trips or a fuse blows quickly, which reduces the chance of a person receiving the shock. The "It stores spare current in the tool so it runs at a steady speed" choice described grounding as storage, but it carries fault current away. The "It makes a damaged cord safe enough to use for short jobs in wet areas" choice treated grounding as a repair for damaged cords, which are removed from service. The "It replaces the need for a GFCI on outlets used outdoors in the rain" choice treated grounding as a replacement for GFCI, but the two protect in different ways.

alternateFinalAssessment.prompt: Why are non-potable water lines marked with labels, colour bands and flow arrows?
choices: To show the crew which pipes are due for repainting next year
To tell visitors the pressure rating of each line in the plant
So a line is not mistaken for drinking water or tapped in error
To satisfy a paint supplier that specifies one colour per pipe size
alternateFinalAssessment.explanation: Marking tells workers and visitors that a line carries water that is not safe to drink, which prevents accidental use and unsafe connections. The "To show the crew which pipes are due for repainting next year" choice treated the marking as a maintenance reminder. The "To tell visitors the pressure rating of each line in the plant" choice treated it as a pressure label. The "To satisfy a paint supplier that specifies one colour per pipe size" choice treated it as a supplier preference.

alternateFinalAssessment.prompt: A fictional operator is bitten by a stray dog while reading a meter at a remote site. Which response fits awareness-level practice?
choices: Clean the wound, report the bite and get medical advice promptly
Skip reporting because a small bite heals without a visit
Cover the bite and finish the route before telling anyone
Wait for symptoms before deciding whether any follow-up is needed
alternateFinalAssessment.explanation: A bite can carry infection or disease, so it is cleaned, reported and assessed by medical staff soon after. The "Skip reporting because a small bite heals without a visit" choice judged the risk by the size of the wound, but a small bite can still carry serious infection or rabies risk. The "Cover the bite and finish the route before telling anyone" choice delayed care and the report for the sake of the route. The "Wait for symptoms before deciding whether any follow-up is needed" choice waited for symptoms, which can appear after the best window for treatment.

alternateFinalAssessment.prompt: Why must equipment brought into a classified flammable-gas area carry a matching rating?
choices: To prove the item passed its bump test and has a fresh battery installed
To make sure a spark inside will not ignite the gas around the item
To show the item is waterproof when it is washed down with a hose
To permit the item to run from a stronger power supply than normal
alternateFinalAssessment.explanation: An explosion-proof or intrinsically safe rating shows the item is built so that a spark or heat inside it does not ignite the surrounding gas. The "To prove the item passed its bump test and has a fresh battery installed" choice confused an ignition rating with a meter check. The "To show the item is waterproof when it is washed down with a hose" choice confused an ignition rating with a washdown rating. The "To permit the item to run from a stronger power supply than normal" choice confused an ignition rating with a power rating.

alternateFinalAssessment.prompt: A fictional operator plans to power a drill outdoors on a damp morning. Which setup fits recognition-level practice?
choices: A long run made by joining two indoor extension cords together
A cord taped over its damage with the ground prong removed so it fits
A rated outdoor cord on a GFCI outlet, kept out of puddles
A cord strung through the doorway and pinched under the closed door
alternateFinalAssessment.explanation: A cord rated for outdoor use on a GFCI-protected outlet, kept out of water, limits both damage to the cord and harm from a ground fault. The "A long run made by joining two indoor extension cords together" choice joined indoor cords that are not rated for damp outdoor use. The "A cord taped over its damage with the ground prong removed so it fits" choice used a damaged cord and defeated the grounding prong. The "A cord strung through the doorway and pinched under the closed door" choice pinched the cord, which damages the insulation.

alternateFinalAssessment.prompt: A fictional operator wants to keep lunch cold at the plant. Which place fits contamination awareness?
choices: The laboratory refrigerator on the shelf beside the sample bottles
A shelf in the chemical room set well back from the doorway
The lab bench next to the reagent bottles that are kept capped
A refrigerator in a clean break area set aside for food
alternateFinalAssessment.explanation: Food belongs in a designated clean area away from samples and chemicals, because contamination reaches the mouth through food, drink and hands. The "The laboratory refrigerator on the shelf beside the sample bottles" choice stored food with samples and reagents, a direct route for contamination. The "A shelf in the chemical room set well back from the doorway" choice treated distance from the door as protection, but chemical vapors and spills still reach the food. The "The lab bench next to the reagent bottles that are kept capped" choice relied on capped bottles, which can leak or be handled with contaminated hands.
